title: HMI Alarms -- Latch & Acknowledge
concept:
An HMI/SCADA alarm must LATCH the moment a condition trips, so a brief fault is
never missed, and stay latched until the operator ACKNOWLEDGES it AND the
condition has cleared. That's a seal-in with an acknowledge:

    IF Alarm_In THEN
        Alarm_Latched := TRUE;         (* trip and hold *)
    ELSIF Ack THEN
        Alarm_Latched := FALSE;        (* clear only when condition is gone *)
    END_IF;

Because the ELSIF only runs when Alarm_In is FALSE, pressing Ack while the fault
is still active does NOT clear it -- exactly what you want.
ab_note: Studio 5000 has ALARM/ALMD instructions with built-in latch + ack; the logic above is the same idea in plain ST for any HMI tag.
siemens_note: TIA Portal WinCC alarms latch in the HMI, but the PLC-side latch/ack logic is identical ST. 'First-out' annunciation extends this by remembering which alarm tripped first.
task:
Given Alarm_In (BOOL, TRUE when abnormal) and Ack (BOOL, operator acknowledge),
drive Alarm_Latched (BOOL):
  - Latch TRUE as soon as Alarm_In is TRUE
  - Clear to FALSE only when Ack is pressed AND Alarm_In has cleared

Use IF Alarm_In ... ELSIF Ack ... END_IF;.

checks.message: Clears on Ack (ELSIF, so only when Alarm_In is FALSE)
Executed: latches, holds unacked, and Ack only clears when the fault is gone
checks.hint: Ack while Alarm_In is still TRUE must NOT clear it (the IF re-latches).

solution:
(* Lesson 12 -- HMI Alarms: Latch & Acknowledge *)

VAR
    Alarm_In      : BOOL;  (* fault condition     -> XIC (as-is): TRUE = fault active *)
    Ack           : BOOL;  (* N.O. acknowledge PB -> XIC (as-is)                     *)
    Alarm_Latched : BOOL;  (* output: latched alarm shown on the HMI                 *)
END_VAR

(* ----- YOUR LOGIC : write your answer between these two lines ----- *)
IF Alarm_In THEN
    Alarm_Latched := TRUE;
ELSIF Ack THEN
    Alarm_Latched := FALSE;
END_IF;
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)
